title: Heat Transfer
standard_code: Grade 7, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: Heat is transferred by conduction, convection and radiation; conductors and insulators; controlling heat transfer in daily life. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 7, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy): conduction, convection and radiation, ways heat moves, conductors and insulators, saving heat and energy and controlling heat transfer. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Heat moves by conduction, convection and radiation.
body_html:
How to think about it

Conduction moves heat through solids (a metal spoon in hot soup). Convection moves heat in liquids and gases as warm fluid rises and cool fluid sinks, as in a pot of boiling water or a sea breeze. Radiation carries heat through empty space, such as from the Sun.

Insulators such as wood, plastic, cloth, foam and still air slow down heat transfer; conductors such as metals let heat flow easily. Light-colored roofs and walls reflect sunlight and keep houses cooler; ceiling fans and open windows let convection carry hot air away.

Example

Why does a metal spoon in hot soup become hot?

Through the solid

Answer: conduction

Example

Why are air conditioners placed high on a wall?

Cool air sinks.

Answer: convection currents spread the cool air

Common mistakes

  • Thinking cold moves into things.
  • Thinking a blanket makes heat.
  • Thinking dark clothes keep you cooler in the sun.

Light colors reflect more sunlight, so less heat is absorbed.

items.q: Jasmine observes a sea breeze blowing toward land on a sunny day. Which kind of heat transfer is this mainly?
items.e: Energy is carried by a moving liquid or gas.

items.q: Dennis observes a heat lamp keeping food warm. Which kind of heat transfer is this mainly?
items.e: Energy travels as light or infrared waves, even through empty space.

items.q: What is the difference between heat and temperature?
c: Temperature is a kind of fuel.
Heat is measured with a ruler.
Temperature measures how hot something is; heat is energy moving from warmer to cooler.
items.e: Heat flows from hot to cold.

Polystyrene foam, because it traps air, a poor conductor.

c: It is made of conducting metal only.
Its vacuum layer stops conduction and convection, and shiny walls reduce radiation.

items.q: What is thermal pollution?
c: warm water released into rivers or lakes that harms aquatic life
items.e: Warm water holds less oxygen.

items.q: Which material is best for oven gloves?

items.q: Why can radiation travel through space but conduction cannot?
c: Radiation is a wave and needs no particles; conduction needs particles.

items.e: Energy moves between objects that are touching.

items.q: What is thermal equilibrium?
c: when objects reach the same temperature and there is no net energy transfer
items.e: No more change.

items.q: What is the difference between temperature and thermal energy?
c: Temperature measures how hot something is; thermal energy also depends on how much material there is.
items.e: A bath at 40 °C has more thermal energy than a cup at 90 °C.

items.q: Why does a metal bench feel colder than a wooden one on the same day?
c: Metal conducts energy away from your hand faster.
Wood is warmer than the air.
items.e: Both are the same temperature.

items.q: Energy is transferred from a hot stove to a pot of water. What happens to the stove's particles near the pot?
items.e: Energy moves from hotter to cooler.

items.q: What is thermal energy?
c: the total kinetic energy of all the particles in an object
items.e: More particles at the same temperature means more thermal energy.

items.q: When you heat water, what happens to its particles?
items.e: Adding energy increases kinetic energy.

items.q: How can planting trees help keep a house cool?
c: Trees shade the house and release water vapor that cools the air.
items.e: Shade reduces air-conditioning use.

items.q: What is the greenhouse effect?
c: a greenhouse on a farm only
gases in the atmosphere trap heat and keep Earth warm
items.e: Without it, Earth would be frozen.

items.q: Which heat source comes from inside Earth?
items.e: Ground-source heat pumps use it.

items.q: In which direction is energy transferred when two objects touch?
c: from the cooler object to the hotter one
from the hotter object to the cooler one
items.e: Until they reach the same temperature.

items.q: Two pots of water get the same amount of heat. Pot A has 1 kg and pot B has 2 kg. Which warms up more?
items.e: Less mass means a bigger temperature change.

items.q: Why do ocean currents and winds move heat around the planet?

items.q: Which is a renewable source of heat?
